The Real Wedding
I lost. Vivaan's book is selling. But nobody believes it. They believe the two of you. That's never happened to me before.
You played my voice to the whole country. My friends don't call anymore. My daughter doesn't call.
My husband wants to come home. To Tara. I can't stop him anymore. I'm asking you... to tell her I'm sorry. She won't hear it from me.
"Tell her yourself. I'll be in the room."
Give her a chance.
"No. You don't get a messenger."
Some doors close.
You keep your promise. Rajiv Kapoor comes home in a wheelchair, and Tara sits on the floor beside him and doesn't let go of his hand for an hour.
The divorce papers, still in your bag. Her signature on one side. Your box still empty.
Amritsar. A small gurdwara. Forty guests, no drones. Dadi in charge of everything. Sid crying into a plate of jalebis.
No contract this time. No clause seven. Just a roti shaped like Sri Lanka, and you.
Finally. A real wedding. The other one had too many cameras and not enough pickle.
Bollywood Wife complete: the fake marriage became a real one. Thank you for playing.
You sign. So does she. In the same room. Then she makes you parathas, badly, and you eat every one.
Divorced. Best friends. Let's see what happens without a contract. Maybe something. Maybe slowly.
Bollywood Wife complete: no contract, no marriage, and a door left open.
You sign. She flies to London. You read her name in the trades: her first film, her own choice. It's very good.
Sometimes, at 2 AM, you make parathas for one.
Bollywood Wife complete: a contract fulfilled, two careers saved. Replay to change how it ends.
